project.purpose: Provider-agnostic observability and optimization layer for AI coding CLIs.
project.primary_goal: Measure how AI CLIs are being used, classify task complexity, compare that complexity with the model/reasoning level used, normalize token telemetry, and later support recommendations, quota warnings and efficient cross-provider handoffs.
project.future_providers: Any provider implemented through the adapter contract.

golden_rule.statement: The public/core project MUST NOT contain, persist, transmit, log, commit, print, or expose personal data, sensitive data, proprietary project content, source-code content, complete prompts, credentials, authentication tokens, API keys, cookies, session identifiers, private endpoints, account identifiers, or provider secrets.
principles: Explicit opt-in for any future content capture
No provider-specific credentials in the core
Safe defaults must work without real credentials

distribution_model.clone_experience: A user must be able to clone the repository and run the non-connected/core functionality without supplying any private information.
distribution_model.credential_policy: Users configure their own provider authentication locally. Credentials never become part of the repository or normalized telemetry.
distribution_model.extension_policy: Users may create their own adapters, bridges, plugins, hooks or integrations without modifying the provider-agnostic core.
configuration_strategy: Environment variables for secrets when required
Non-secret local configuration file for preferences
.env.example containing variable names and fake placeholders only
Provider-specific adapters isolated from the core
Secret validation before an adapter starts
Never serialize secrets into telemetry events

architecture.behavior: Observe and measure first. Do not automatically change provider, model, reasoning level, or user workflow.

adapters.responsibility: Translate provider/CLI-specific events into the universal event contract.
adapters.rule: Provider-specific behavior must remain inside its adapter.

storage.content_policy: Store normalized metadata only; never raw prompts, raw responses, source code, or credentials.

crm.note: The future CRM/dashboard consumes normalized telemetry; it must not require changes to the core contract.

universal_complexity_model.intent: Represent required reasoning effort independently of provider-specific model names or controls.

roadmap.name: Observe
deliverables: CLI-visible lightweight feedback where technically supported

roadmap.name: Recommend
deliverables: Quota/credit warnings where providers expose reliable data

roadmap.name: Optimize and Handoff
deliverables: Provider comparison based on observed user workloads
Optimization recommendations based on empirical telemetry

implementation_guardrails: Do not assume equivalent provider features when documentation does not confirm equivalence.
Unsupported telemetry fields must be null rather than inferred.
Do not scrape or bypass provider security controls to obtain usage data.
Do not capture prompt or response content merely to improve classification.
Prefer deterministic local heuristics for the first classifier so classification itself does not consume AI tokens.
Any future AI-based classifier must be optional and measurable.
Adapters must fail safely when credentials, hooks or telemetry are unavailable.
The repository must include synthetic examples so contributors can develop without real provider accounts.

handoff_to_codex.first_milestone: Create the repository skeleton, universal event JSON Schema, privacy-safe SQLite schema, adapter interface, synthetic fixtures and tests before implementing any real provider connection.
acceptance_criteria: Core runs without any provider credentials.
Synthetic events for all three initial providers validate against the same schema.
No sensitive-data field exists in the normalized event contract.
Secrets and telemetry databases are ignored by Git.
A contributor can add a new provider through the adapter interface without changing the core event model.
Tests reject known credential patterns from fixtures intended for persistence.
